title: I am working on a voxel ARPG and I'm having so much fun but I'm lost as hell
author: ramigb
selftext:
I've been trying to make my own games for over 20 years. As a software engineer, I'd get excited, build a couple of levels, then eventually give up. Now, with two young daughters and even less free time, I want to finally make games we can enjoy together.

With the limited time I have every day, I needed a way to rekindle this hobby, so I created multiple tools ([which are open source and free](https://ramigb.github.io/epoptes/)) to allow me to task LLMs to build autonomously and for me to come back when it's time to try the game and give directions.

I do not plan to release my game(s) as commercial products. I want to play them by myself, with my daughters, and eventually just release them as open source. This example I share with you today is a fun one that is super rough around the edges, but I like it a lot because it demonstrates that long-horizon, agent-driven game development is feasible in my setup. My latest run lasted over 20 hours, using Claude Pro alongside Codex, Devin, and Agy plans to carry out development tasks autonomously, with me providing feedback and direction between iterations.

I lack the visual creativity some of the beautiful folks around here have. I am more of an audio guy, always have been. In this particular video, I am focusing more on the mechanics before I implement the narrative.

Final note: You guys are amazing. What you are doing is super creative. I feel very inspired by a lot of the content here. Don't let anyone take that away from you.
